title: Formal Lean Proof of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (Zero-Free Strip Re(s) > 7/8)
aiSystem: OpenAI Internal Frontier Math Model + Lean 4
whyItMatters: OpenAI’s internal model proved the 167-year-old Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis—confining all nontrivial zeta zeros to Re(s) ∈ [1/8, 7/8] in Lean 4—unlocking scores of prime-distribution consequences.
summary: As the centerpiece of OpenAI’s October 6, 2026 mathematical release (Family 003), an unreleased internal OpenAI model produced two proofs of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: a 199-page Lean-formalized proof showing no nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have Re(s) > 7/8 (confining all zeros to [1/8, 7/8]), and a shorter 49-page proof for [1/12, 11/12]. Unpacked by number theorists Maksym Radziwiłł, Alexander Dunn, and Peter Sarnak and profiled by Quanta Magazine, the AI unexpectedly linked metaplectic forms with a 2021 Dunn–Radziwiłł formula to establish the first fixed-strip zero-free half-plane—described at the time as “the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far” prior to Alpöge and Claude’s November 20 full Riemann Hypothesis proof.
technicalHighlights: Proved the first unconditional fixed zero-free half-plane Re(s) > 7/8 for the Riemann zeta function (with Lean 4 formalization) plus a 49-page argument for Re(s) > 11/12.
Autonomously identified an overlooked family of metaplectic forms and synthesized it with a 2021 formula of Alexander Dunn and Maksym Radziwiłł.
Unpacked by leading analytic number theorists (Radziwiłł, Dunn, Sarnak) and spurred immediate arXiv follow-ups (e.g., arXiv:2610.12234 tightening the zero-free half-plane).
caveats: Experts noted the raw AI manuscripts were poorly written by journal standards (leading researchers to focus first on unpacking the 49-page 11/12 version), and Peter Sarnak cautioned full human refereeing is required for canonical theorem status; subsequently superseded in strength by Alpöge & Claude’s Nov 20, 2026 Lean proof of the full Riemann Hypothesis.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settled the 167-year-old Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis, establishing the first fixed exponent below 1 for the prime-counting error term.
scoreRationale.ripple: Converted scores of RH-conditional results across number theory, geometry, and TCS into unconditional theorems and demonstrated creative cross-field synthesis.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by a Lean 4 formalization for the 7/8 bound plus independent technical unpacking by Dunn, Radziwiłł, and Sarnak, though formal journal publication is pending.
scoreRationale.velocity: Generated in a single automated compute sweep and unpacked by leading number theorists within two weeks.
